problems.problem: A duplicate OTH Knowledge HTTP facade and a colliding test file were written before the branch state was re-checked. An equivalent implementation already existed on the working branch, committed concurrently.
problems.root_cause: Implementation began without re-running branch/status inspection at the start of the build phase; the working directory had moved to vps/oth-mcp-20260830.
problems.resolution: Both files removed. Consolidated onto the existing implementation, which is committed, better placed and accompanied by an MCP server. Existing suites re-run and green.
problems.lesson: Re-verify branch and working-tree state immediately before implementing, not only at session start.

problems.problem: projects/oth-mcp/server.js declares its own TOOLS array and does not consult lib/mcp-capabilities.js.
problems.assessment: Not a duplicate authorization system — the registry governs which tools an executor skill may name, while the server's TOOLS is the client-facing surface. They are different concerns.
problems.resolution: Recorded, not refactored. Rewiring freshly written, tested code discovered late in the session was judged the riskier action.

outcome: Reconciliation prevented three of four candidate components from being built. MYTHOS RECON was not built because the Status Center review engine already is that layer. The knowledge facade was not built twice — the duplicate was withdrawn. Only the genuinely missing discovery feeder and one capability declaration were added.
next_action: Owner decisions: (1) classify othoth77/spy, now surfacing as NEW_DISCOVERY; (2) decide whether oth-mcp/server.js should consult lib/mcp-capabilities.js; (3) enable the oth-knowledge capability declaration when the facade is deployed.
